Hazlo en 90 minutos, sin mirar las soluciones.
PAU 2027 · Modelo 1 de Escolapedia

Inglés II

Read the text and answer all the questions in English. Time: 90 minutes.

Nombre: ______________________   Fecha: ___________   Nota: ______

Is the four-day week the future of work?

When a group of companies in the United Kingdom agreed to try a four-day working week for six months, many experts expected productivity to fall. Employees would work 80% of their usual hours but keep 100% of their salary. The results surprised almost everyone. Most companies reported that their income stayed the same or even increased slightly, and the majority decided to continue with the new schedule after the trial had finished.

Workers said they felt less tired and stressed. Many used their extra day to exercise, spend time with their families or deal with tasks such as medical appointments, which they had previously squeezed into busy weekdays. Some managers noticed that fewer people took sick days, and that it became easier to attract new staff.

However, the model is not suitable for every sector. Hospitals, schools and restaurants cannot simply close one day a week, so they would need to hire more people to cover the shifts, which would increase costs. Critics also point out that some employees felt under pressure to do the same amount of work in fewer hours, and that meetings were sometimes cut so drastically that communication suffered.

Supporters argue that the real lesson is not about the number of days, but about how time is used. If unnecessary meetings and distractions are reduced, they say, people can achieve more in less time and have a better life outside work.

  1. Are these statements TRUE or FALSE? Justify your answers with evidence from the text. a) Experts predicted that the trial would be a success. b) Most companies continued with the four-day week. c) The model would be cheaper for hospitals. (1,5 p.)

  2. Answer these questions in your own words. a) How did workers use their free day? b) What problems did critics mention? (2 p.)

  3. Find words or expressions in the text that mean: a) the amount of work done in a period of time (paragraph 1); b) put with difficulty into a small space (paragraph 2); c) people who say something is wrong (paragraph 3); d) very strongly, in an extreme way (paragraph 3). (1 p.)

  4. Complete the second sentence so that it means the same as the first. a) «We will continue with the new schedule», the manager said. → The manager said that… b) Workers felt less tired, although they did the same job. → Despite… c) The companies didn't expect such good results. → Such good results… (1,5 p.)

  5. Writing (120-150 words): «Should students have a four-day school week? Give your opinion with reasons and examples.» (4 p.)

Soluciones y criterios de corrección

  1. a) FALSE: «many experts expected productivity to fall». b) TRUE: «the majority decided to continue with the new schedule after the trial had finished». c) FALSE: «they would need to hire more people to cover the shifts, which would increase costs». (0,5 each; no mark without justification.)
  2. a) They did exercise, spent time with their families and did personal tasks, like going to the doctor, that they used to do on working days. b) Some sectors would need more staff and more money; some employees had to do the same work in less time and felt stressed; communication was worse because there were too few meetings. (1 point each: content 0,5, own words and correctness 0,5.)
  3. a) productivity; b) squeezed; c) critics; d) drastically. (0,25 each.)
  4. a) The manager said that they would continue with the new schedule. b) Despite doing the same job, workers felt less tired. / Despite the fact that they did the same job… c) Such good results were not expected by the companies. (0,5 each.)
  5. Assessment: task fulfilment and content (1), organisation and cohesion: paragraphs and connectors (1), grammar (1), vocabulary (1). Model answer (≈140 words): Nowadays, some people suggest that students should only go to school four days a week. In my opinion, this idea has advantages, but it would cause more problems than benefits. On the one hand, a free day could help students rest, practise sports or study at their own pace. Moreover, families could spend more time together. On the other hand, the school year would have to be longer or each day would be much more intense, and teenagers already have very long timetables. In addition, many parents work five days a week, so younger children would need someone to look after them. To sum up, I believe that, instead of reducing the number of days, schools should organise time better, with fewer exams on the same day and more practical activities.
